original.target_description: Unassigned original side; no original primary source inspected.

replication.target_description: Relationship between attempting to solve problems prior to instruction and awareness of knowledge gaps, in the context of students’ conceptual understanding.

reported_success.quote:
While we failed to replicate the findings of Loibl and Rummel (2014a) in our conceptual
replication study, our results do not contradict the theoretical assumptions made by Loibl
and Rummel.

notes:
Identity verified from supplied text: matching title Can failure be made productive also in Bayesian reasoning? A conceptual replication study, Katharina Loibl and Timo Leuders, DOI 10.1007/s11251-024-09670-y, ORIGINAL RESEARCH, online 12 July 2024, final issue Instructional Science (2025) 53:1739–1758. Primary replication research report with full methods, results, discussion and references. No PDF supplied. Original side and unassigned fields are placeholders only. Target ambiguous: the neutral description combines attempted problem solving, awareness and conceptual understanding, without naming a unique measured test. Separate candidates are conceptual-learning order-of-phases ANOVA (hypothesis 1a), its rank-transformed sensitivity analysis, exploratory solution-attempt frequencies and discussion-level awareness explanation. No target inferred from repeated descriptions, row order or numeric matching. Candidate conceptual ANOVA: F(1,71) = 0.12, p = .73, partial eta squared = 0.002; sensitivity F(1,71) = 0.06, p = .81, partial eta squared = 0.001. Candidate conceptual-model N = 75 (Table 7); exploratory PS-first subgroup N = 38. Neither N is assigned to unresolved target. Evidence: One ANOVA with the dependent variable conceptual
knowledge outcome tested hypothesis 1a (main effect of order of phases), hypothesis 2
(main effect of type of instruction), and hypothesis 3 (interaction). | Out of the 38 students, 31 students generated only one solution attempt, 6 students gen-
erated two solution attempts, and 1 student generated three solution attempts. | One reason for the students’ limited problem-
solving processes may be that students did not become aware of their knowledge gaps.
